AI Builders Digest — 2026-11-10

X / TWITTER

Swyx (Latent Space / AI Engineer)

Latent Space / AI Engineer host Swyx amplified Will Brown's line that "2027 is gonna be about engines," pointed people who want the how to Monaco VP of FDE Pauline Brunet, and flagged a special Latent Space episode for the AI Engineer YouTube channel hitting one million subscribers (Stanford / Monaco guest Mihail Eric; remixed below).

Latent Space / AI Engineer 主持人 Swyx 转发 Will Brown 的判断：“2027 is gonna be about engines”；想知道怎么落地的人，他指向 Monaco VP of FDE Pauline Brunet；并预告 Latent Space 为 AI Engineer YouTube 频道破百万订阅做的特辑（嘉宾为 Stanford / Monaco 的 Mihail Eric；下方有 remix）。

https://x.com/swyx/status/2119611058881192187

https://x.com/willcb/status/2119250590337470728

https://x.com/swyx/status/2119543788192600450

https://x.com/aiDotEngineer/status/2082159947236655311

https://x.com/swyx/status/2119550477629379009

https://x.com/latentspacepod/status/2119550367222653193

Nan Yu (Product, Codex, OpenAI)

OpenAI Codex product builder Nan Yu argues you should pick "dumbest" over "simplest": simple is something you iterate toward, dumb is the correct starting point so you do not outsmart yourself. Across software, choose the dumbest architecture and design that works; being clever forces users to match your cleverness. With AI, software got a lot easier if you know what you want to build and a lot harder if you do not: clarity lets you straight-shot a solution, while lack of clarity ships junk at high cost (pre-AI you often shipped nothing, which he calls an improvement over expensive junk).

OpenAI Codex 产品负责人 Nan Yu 主张选 “dumbest” 而不是 “simplest”：simple 是迭代出来的终点，dumb 才是正确起点，否则你会把自己绕进去。软件各处都应选能干活的最笨架构与设计；太 clever 意味着用户也得同样 clever 才能理解。有了 AI，你若知道要建什么，软件会容易很多；若不知道，反而更难：有清晰目标可以直接打穿方案，没有清晰目标就会高成本堆出一堆 junk（前 AI 时代常常什么都发不出去，他认为那反而比昂贵的 junk 更好）。

https://x.com/thenanyu/status/2119493015190249556

https://x.com/ewgenekim/status/2119468655205663115

https://x.com/thenanyu/status/2119462979179892925

https://x.com/jlongster/status/2119278726886339004

https://x.com/thenanyu/status/2119462224721002560

Guillermo Rauch (CEO, Vercel)

Vercel CEO Guillermo Rauch shipped a WebGL2 + Web Audio physical simulation of a record player at vinyl-gl.vercel.app: audio is converted into groove geometry, a simulated stylus rides the walls 384,000 times a second, and crackle, pops, wow/flutter, and dull inner grooves fall out as natural byproducts. Public-domain / CC songs; code linked to remix.

Vercel CEO Guillermo Rauch 用 WebGL2 + Web Audio 做了一个黑胶唱机物理仿真（vinyl-gl.vercel.app）：把音频转成沟槽几何，模拟唱针以每秒 384,000 次贴壁运动，噼啪声、wow/flutter、内圈发闷都是仿真自然产物。曲目为公有领域 / CC；代码可 remix。

https://x.com/rauchg/status/2119536313712230802

https://vinyl-gl.vercel.app/

Aaron Levie (CEO, Box)

Box CEO Aaron Levie says we are leaving chat-paced AI (output roughly at the rate you can talk back) for a regime where you set a problem for agent swarms that fan out arbitrarily large parallel work: productivity gains move from maybe 20-50% to gains without a clear upper limit. Coding already showed it; next cyber, science, and life sciences look like domains where more agents reviewing more things qualitatively change outcomes. Brains still equate time invested with output; that correlation is breaking as compute becomes the flex variable.

Box CEO Aaron Levie 认为我们正离开“聊天节奏”的 AI（产出大致跟你来回对话的速度绑定），进入你可以给 agent swarm 丢问题、让它们并行摊开任意大体量工作的阶段：生产力提升从大约 20-50% 变成没有清晰上限。编程领域已经演示过；接下来网络安全、科学、生命科学等，更像是“更多 agent 审查更多东西就会质变”的空间。人脑仍习惯用投入时间衡量产出；当 compute 成为可伸缩变量，这种相关性正在永久断裂。

Separately he advises checking back every 3 to 6 months on what was impossible before: the last half-year of computer/tool use, less context rot, better reasoning, multimodality, and deeper domain expertise means agents can drive existing systems via APIs (security feeds, IT workflows, data migration, CAD) instead of generating everything from whole cloth, which creates leverage for autonomous collaborators in every job function.

另外他建议每 3 到 6 个月回来试一次曾经做不到的事：过去半年在 computer/tool use、更少 context rot、更强推理、多模态与更深领域专长上的进步，意味着 agent 可以经由 API 操控既有系统（安全数据源、IT 工作流、数据迁移、CAD），而不必一切从零生成，从而给每个岗位带来自主协作者杠杆。

https://x.com/levie/status/2119592025440092192

https://x.com/levie/status/2119502716770902234

Ryo Lu (Designer, Cursor)

Cursor designer Ryo Lu posted his full AI Engineer Shanghai talk: "when we can do anything, do we still know what we want?" Slides handmade in Keynote, with Chinese and English subtitles.

Cursor 设计师 Ryo Lu 放出 AI Engineer 上海演讲全文：“when we can do anything, do we still know what we want?” 每页幻灯片手做于 Keynote，中英字幕齐全。

https://x.com/ryolu_/status/2119586846657454152

Garry Tan (President & CEO, Y Combinator)

Y Combinator President & CEO Garry Tan says once frontier models make software so easy to change, ordinary bugs become "a little bit unbearable," and personal just-in-time software starts to look inevitable. He also amplified the Demis Hassabis line that one person who really understands AI will outperform an entire startup team, and that builders with AI will run companies at a tenth of the headcount ("you're really going to want your own software factory"). Separately, his gstack-evals project tried to replicate a Jev Engineering article and also tested particle-1; he reports the article replicates and particle-1 is even better.

Y Combinator 总裁兼 CEO Garry Tan 说：一旦你意识到前沿模型让软件极容易被改写，普通 bug 会开始让人“有点受不了”，与此同时个人即时软件（personal just-in-time software）看起来不可避免。他还放大 Demis Hassabis 的判断：真正懂 AI 的一个人会跑赢整个 startup 团队，用 AI 构建的人将以十分之一人数运营公司（“you're really going to want your own software factory”）。另外，他的 gstack-evals 项目尝试复现一篇 Jev Engineering 文章并试了 particle-1；结果是文章可复现，且 particle-1 更好。

https://x.com/garrytan/status/2119612084220842483

https://x.com/garrytan/status/2119615647592395037

https://x.com/RoundtableSpace/status/2119093769991774480

https://x.com/garrytan/status/2119624260675350605

https://x.com/Mr_Buzzoni/status/2104783226833186920

https://x.com/i/article/2104561908137283584

Zara Zhang (Builder / Follow Builders)

Builder Zara Zhang says she has almost stopped using "vibe coding" because it implies low effort and AI slop, while people often put heart and soul into work even with AI coding tools; the two are not contradictory, and the industry needs a better word. Separately: the joy of building comes from the collision between how predictably technology behaves and how unpredictably humans behave.

Builder Zara Zhang 说她几乎不再用 “vibe coding”：这个词带有负标签，暗示没下功夫、只是 AI slop；但很多人即使用 AI 编码工具，仍把心血放进作品里，两者并不矛盾，行业需要更好的词。另：做产品的乐趣，来自技术行为的可预期，与人类行为的不可预期之间的碰撞。

https://x.com/zarazhangrui/status/2119592080318341128

https://x.com/zarazhangrui/status/2119342420412510686

Nikunj Kothari (Partner, FPV Ventures)

FPV Ventures partner Nikunj Kothari lists SF vocabulary to drop if you want real meetings (swap notes, synergies, pick your brain, networking, "san fran," grab coffee if you're free): show your work instead, via a pointed cold email, a five-line DM, a shipped side project, or a meetup you organize. Even in the AI era he still sees so much slop that visible effort makes him go out of his way; busy people still have 15 minutes if you give them a reason.

FPV Ventures 合伙人 Nikunj Kothari 列出想在 SF 真正约到人时该删掉的词（swap notes、synergies、pick your brain、networking、“san fran”、grab coffee if you're free）：用作品说话，一封有想法的冷邮件、五句到位的 DM、一个已上线的 side project，或你自己办的 meetup。即便在 AI 时代，他仍每天看到大量 slop，所以只要看到有人真下功夫，就会特意去见；再忙的人也有 15 分钟，前提是你给了理由。

https://x.com/nikunj/status/2119670529254981756

PODCASTS

[One Million AI Engineer Special] How Stanford Teaches AI-Native Engineering — Mihail Eric, Monaco

**The Takeaway:** A well-trained AI-native engineer is still one of the most useful assets a company can hire, but the floor is now near senior: vanilla "do the thing" prompting does not scale to million-line codebases; you need research-proposal-plan workflows, ruthless context engineering, and ambition above photo-to-app demos.

**要点：** 训练有素的 AI-native 工程师仍是公司最管用的资产之一，但入门门槛已接近 senior：只会 vanilla “帮我做这件事” 的 prompting，撑不住百万行代码库；你需要 research→proposal→plan 工作流、严格的 context engineering，以及高于“拍照变 App”的野心。

Mihail Eric is Adjunct Professor at Stanford (CS 146S, The Modern Software Developer, second offering) and Head of AI at Monaco, a Series B San Francisco company building an all-in-one AI-native sales platform. Latent Space hosts the conversation as a one-million-subscriber special for the AI Engineer YouTube channel. The course started as an idea in November 2024 (inspired in part by Chip Hieatt's ML systems class; ASR spelling), first taught fall 2025, and is refreshed now that autonomous coding agents have jumped hard: last year's syllabus was more of an SDLC survey of agent products; this year principles are solidifying around careful context engineering and architecture for complex work. It is not a beginner CS replacement; algorithms remain prerequisites. Week-one message to students: every company needs you, but showing up as a Google-style L3 is no longer enough.

Mihail Eric 是 Stanford 兼职教授（CS 146S The Modern Software Developer，第二届），也是 Monaco 的 Head of AI；Monaco 是旧金山一家 Series B、做一体式 AI-native 销售平台的公司。Latent Space 把这次访谈做成 AI Engineer YouTube 频道破百万订阅特辑。课程萌芽于 2024 年 11 月（部分受 Chip Hieatt 的 ML systems 课启发；ASR 拼写），2025 年秋季首开，如今因自主 coding agent 暴涨而大改：去年更像是 SDLC 各环节 agent 产品巡礼，今年原则开始凝固，聚焦仔细的 context engineering，以及用设计/架构扛复杂任务。它不是入门 CS 替代课，算法等仍是先修。第一周对学生的话：每家公司都需要你，但只以 Google 口径的 L3 入场已经不够。

On harnesses versus weights, he walks students through intercepting coding-agent traffic (system / plan / compaction prompts). Claude Code's early bet on fewer Swiss Army knife tools (Bash, SQL) helped it explode; its famously long system prompt has been cut and grown in cycles as behaviors move into model weights, which is the community seesaw between investing in the harness and investing in the model. For large unfamiliar codebases he pushes a REPIT-style loop (research, proposal with alternatives for a human decision, plan/spec, implementation, tests), functionally close to Dex-style RPI: almost nobody he interviews has progressed past vanilla prompting, and that is exactly what fails at Google-scale repos. Fan-out makes it worse: sub-agents need the right slice of context, then expand/contract cycles fight over-tuning to random old comments.

在 harness 与模型权重之间，他带着学生拦截 coding agent 流量（system / plan / compaction prompts）。Claude Code 早期押注更少、更强的瑞士军刀工具（Bash、SQL）助其爆发；其出名的超长 system prompt 经历砍了又长、长了又砍，因为行为逐渐写进模型权重，这也是社区在“投 harness”与“投模型”之间反复横跳的缩影。面对巨大陌生代码库，他推 REPIT 式循环（research、带备选方案供人拍板的 proposal、plan/spec、实现、测试），功能上接近 Dex 风格的 RPI：他面试到的人几乎都还停在 vanilla prompting，而这在 Google 体量仓库里必然翻车。Fan-out 更糟：sub-agent 需要正确的上下文切片，随后在 expand/contract 里和“被很久以前一句随口话带偏”作斗争。

At Monaco the buy-versus-build rule is "buy to learn and build to keep." They run Monocoder (on Coder.com) for isolated multi-agent long-horizon coding, plus Hal, a Slack bot that shifts personality across SRE, customer success, and QA depending on who is asking. Code review is the rare case they stayed on a vendor: an early bake-off (CodeRabbit, Graphite, Ellipsis, and others) found nothing crossing the usefulness bar; later Devin was adopted organically after a second look, with engineers asking to be added rather than leadership pushing. Closing advice from the room: raise ambition (writing a browser beats snapping a photo into an app), and make benchmarks plus rigorous engineering write-ups if you want doors open at frontier and agent labs.

在 Monaco，买与建的原则是 “buy to learn and build to keep”。他们用基于 Coder.com 的 Monocoder 做隔离的多 agent 长程编码，再用 Slack 机器人 Hal 按对象切换 SRE / customer success / QA 人格。代码审查是少数继续买的：早年横向评测（CodeRabbit、Graphite、Ellipsis 等）没有产品跨过“立刻有用”的线；后来再看 Devin，是工程师自发要求加权限，而不是领导强推。收尾建议：把野心拉高（写浏览器远胜拍照变 App），并去做 benchmarks 与有严谨度的工程博文，这能敲开前沿实验室与 agent 实验室的门。

"Hey, I really believe that every company needs you, but the floor is much higher."
“嘿，我真的相信每家公司都需要你，但地板已经高得多了。”

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=dpY7YzZo4kE

**要点：** 训练有素的 AI-native 工程师仍是公司最管用的资产之一，但入门门槛已接近 senior：只会 vanilla “帮我做这件事” 的 prompting，撑不住百万行代码库；你需要 research→proposal→plan 工作流、严格的 context engineering，以及高于“拍照变 App”的野心。

Mihail Eric is Adjunct Professor at Stanford (CS 146S, The Modern Software Developer, second offering) and Head of AI at Monaco, a Series B San Francisco company building an all-in-one AI-native sales platform. Latent Space hosts the conversation as a one-million-subscriber special for the AI Engineer YouTube channel. The course started as an idea in November 2024 (inspired in part by Chip Hieatt's ML systems class; ASR spelling), first taught fall 2025, and is refreshed now that autonomous coding agents have jumped hard: last year's syllabus was more of an SDLC survey of agent products; this year principles are solidifying around careful context engineering and architecture for complex work. It is not a beginner CS replacement; algorithms remain prerequisites. Week-one message to students: every company needs you, but showing up as a Google-style L3 is no longer enough.

Mihail Eric 是 Stanford 兼职教授（CS 146S The Modern Software Developer，第二届），也是 Monaco 的 Head of AI；Monaco 是旧金山一家 Series B、做一体式 AI-native 销售平台的公司。Latent Space 把这次访谈做成 AI Engineer YouTube 频道破百万订阅特辑。课程萌芽于 2024 年 11 月（部分受 Chip Hieatt 的 ML systems 课启发；ASR 拼写），2025 年秋季首开，如今因自主 coding agent 暴涨而大改：去年更像是 SDLC 各环节 agent 产品巡礼，今年原则开始凝固，聚焦仔细的 context engineering，以及用设计/架构扛复杂任务。它不是入门 CS 替代课，算法等仍是先修。第一周对学生的话：每家公司都需要你，但只以 Google 口径的 L3 入场已经不够。

On harnesses versus weights, he walks students through intercepting coding-agent traffic (system / plan / compaction prompts). Claude Code's early bet on fewer Swiss Army knife tools (Bash, SQL) helped it explode; its famously long system prompt has been cut and grown in cycles as behaviors move into model weights, which is the community seesaw between investing in the harness and investing in the model. For large unfamiliar codebases he pushes a REPIT-style loop (research, proposal with alternatives for a human decision, plan/spec, implementation, tests), functionally close to Dex-style RPI: almost nobody he interviews has progressed past vanilla prompting, and that is exactly what fails at Google-scale repos. Fan-out makes it worse: sub-agents need the right slice of context, then expand/contract cycles fight over-tuning to random old comments.

在 harness 与模型权重之间，他带着学生拦截 coding agent 流量（system / plan / compaction prompts）。Claude Code 早期押注更少、更强的瑞士军刀工具（Bash、SQL）助其爆发；其出名的超长 system prompt 经历砍了又长、长了又砍，因为行为逐渐写进模型权重，这也是社区在“投 harness”与“投模型”之间反复横跳的缩影。面对巨大陌生代码库，他推 REPIT 式循环（research、带备选方案供人拍板的 proposal、plan/spec、实现、测试），功能上接近 Dex 风格的 RPI：他面试到的人几乎都还停在 vanilla prompting，而这在 Google 体量仓库里必然翻车。Fan-out 更糟：sub-agent 需要正确的上下文切片，随后在 expand/contract 里和“被很久以前一句随口话带偏”作斗争。

At Monaco the buy-versus-build rule is "buy to learn and build to keep." They run Monocoder (on Coder.com) for isolated multi-agent long-horizon coding, plus Hal, a Slack bot that shifts personality across SRE, customer success, and QA depending on who is asking. Code review is the rare case they stayed on a vendor: an early bake-off (CodeRabbit, Graphite, Ellipsis, and others) found nothing crossing the usefulness bar; later Devin was adopted organically after a second look, with engineers asking to be added rather than leadership pushing. Closing advice from the room: raise ambition (writing a browser beats snapping a photo into an app), and make benchmarks plus rigorous engineering write-ups if you want doors open at frontier and agent labs.

在 Monaco，买与建的原则是 “buy to learn and build to keep”。他们用基于 Coder.com 的 Monocoder 做隔离的多 agent 长程编码，再用 Slack 机器人 Hal 按对象切换 SRE / customer success / QA 人格。代码审查是少数继续买的：早年横向评测（CodeRabbit、Graphite、Ellipsis 等）没有产品跨过“立刻有用”的线；后来再看 Devin，是工程师自发要求加权限，而不是领导强推。收尾建议：把野心拉高（写浏览器远胜拍照变 App），并去做 benchmarks 与有严谨度的工程博文，这能敲开前沿实验室与 agent 实验室的门。
